single_hypothesis: FP32 wide rows with 8192 < D <= 16384 seed the full-y process tile at 8192 instead of 4096 so the UB budget buys fewer tile rounds rather than more resident y rows.
SHARED_BASELINE_LIMITATION: wide-FP32 invRms nondeterminism (~0.8% run-to-run) in ProcessWideFp32FullCacheRows

correctness_detail.fp16_wide: 3-14 elements Inf vs reference, IDENTICAL on parent and candidate (delta 0); deterministic run-to-run
correctness_detail.fp32_wide_D_gt_8192: Fails vs reference on BOTH parent and candidate; run-to-run NONDETERMINISTIC (same binary, same input, different invRms)

determinism_probe.method: two separate processes of the same binary, same input, compare full output dumps
determinism_probe.finding: ProcessWideFp32FullCacheRows produces an invRms that varies by ~0.8% across runs and sits ~0.5-2% off a double-precision reference. FP16/BF16 wide paths are deterministic; BF16 output quantisation hides the same-scale invRms drift (max_abs=0 after bf16 rounding).

ofat_numeric_safety.untouched_cells_parent_vs_candidate_delt: 0 (bit-identical) for fp16/bf16 all tested D and fp32 D=8192
ofat_numeric_safety.change_domain_fp32_D12288_D16384: parent-vs-candidate delta (max_abs ~0.09) sits INSIDE the same-binary run-to-run noise floor (~0.09); cannot separate change effect from parent nondeterminism
ofat_numeric_safety.note: FP32 D=32768 is NOT in the change domain but shows the same ~0.09 delta, confirming the delta is dominated by parent nondeterminism rather than by this revision
